Description: The technique used to reprogram source cells into pluripotent stem cells or directly into another cell type.
Valid Values: Sendai virus, episomal vectors, retroviral transduction, lentiviral transduction, mRNA transfection, piggyBac transposon, chemical reprogramming, adenoviral vectors, protein transduction, microRNA-based reprogramming, minicircle vectors

Description: Transient transfection is the introduction of foreign nucleic acids into eukaryotic cells resulting in temporary expression of the introduced genes, without integration into the host genome.

Non-viral transfection methods rely on physical or chemical means to introduce nucleic acids into cells without the use of viral vectors. Non-viral transfection methods are often preferred for their safety and ease of use, as they do not involve the complexities and potential risks associated with viral vectors, at the cost of lower transfection efficiency and specificity.
Stable transfection method involving the transgene introduction into the cells of interest using engineered retroviral particles.

Adenoviral particles can transduce both replicating and non-dividing cells. Adenoviral DNA does not integrate into the host genome, but rather, resides episomally in the host nucleus.
